fit: concentrated chicken breast dipeptides and weekly ordinary fatigue in healthy adults
assessment: The 400 mg beverage arm favored lower weekly fatigue VAS at weeks 2–8. The Chalder comparison favored it only at week 2, and objective performance was inconclusive. The study does not test a cooked-meat serving or Parkinson fatigue.

fit: chicken breast extract and sprint performance in healthy adults
assessment: Acid–base markers differed. Total and mean sprint power did not separate at the reported threshold, and fatigue severity in Parkinson disease was outside the comparison.

fit: dipeptide content across cuts and sealed liquid retort heating
assessment: The meat contains anserine and carnosine; similar retained content across test conditions supports material identity only. Ordinary poaching, absorption and fatigue were not measured.

fit: home-prepared chicken broth and short intense cycling in healthy trained men
assessment: Mean power favored broth in a 13-person crossover analysis. Red-cell glutathione and acid–base comparisons did not resolve the mechanism. A broth serving and exercise output differ from poached meat and Parkinson fatigue.

fit: observational poultry substitution and composite frailty in older women
assessment: Poultry substitution did not separate clearly for total frailty. The individual fatigue component analysis concerns red meat, with no isolated chicken or Parkinson fatigue estimate.

fit: whole steamed chicken and matched-energy control in a registered four-arm older-women trial
assessment: The methods use steamed chicken. Whole lean mass increased with chicken against the carbohydrate comparator, but Table 3 does not show an added maximal-contraction benefit on the training background. A secondary report shares the cohort. Neither measures Parkinson fatigue.

fit: cross-sectional dietary recall and presence of fatigue in Parkinson disease
assessment: A measured-fat contrast concerns total intake and the presence of fatigue. Individual poultry exposure, cooking method and fatigue severity are unavailable in the reported comparison.

fit: culinary patent applicant's small ordinal tasting report without patient-specific measurements
assessment: The patent describes a weak favorable repeated-tasting rating for conventional chicken baeksuk and stronger wording for a modified duck dish. No response appeared at the early check. The modified chicken test concerned palatability, and no Parkinson fatigue or controlled effect can be assessed.
